educationalContent.title: What is BMI?
paragraphs: Body Mass Index (BMI) is a numerical value calculated from your weight and height. Developed by Belgian mathematician Adolphe Quetelet in the 1830s, it has become one of the most widely used screening tools for potential weight-related health issues.
The formula is: BMI = weight (kg) / height (m)². For example, a person weighing 70 kg and 1.75 m tall has a BMI of 22.9.
The World Health Organization classifies BMI into categories: Underweight (below 18.5), Normal (18.5-24.9), Overweight (25-29.9), and Obese (30+).

While BMI is useful for screening, it has limitations. It doesn't distinguish between muscle and fat mass, which means athletes may have a high BMI despite being healthy. It also doesn't account for fat distribution or age-related changes in body composition.

faqs.question: What is a healthy BMI?
faqs.answer: A healthy BMI for adults is typically between 18.5 and 24.9. However, 'healthy' can vary based on age, muscle mass, ethnicity, and individual factors.

faqs.question: How accurate is BMI?
faqs.answer: BMI is reasonably accurate for most people but can be misleading for athletes, pregnant women, elderly individuals, and those with high muscle mass.

faqs.question: How often should I check my BMI?
faqs.answer: For most adults, monthly checks are sufficient. If actively trying to change weight, weekly monitoring can help track progress.

faqs.question: Does BMI differ for men and women?
faqs.answer: The calculation and categories are the same, but women typically have more body fat than men at the same BMI.

faqs.question: How do I calculate BMI for children?
faqs.answer: Children's BMI uses the same formula but is interpreted using age and sex-specific growth charts as percentiles.

educationalContent.title: How Mortgage Payments Work
paragraphs: Your monthly mortgage payment (PITI) consists of four main components: Principal (loan repayment), Interest (cost of borrowing), Taxes (property taxes), and Insurance (homeowner's insurance).
Early in your mortgage, most of your payment goes toward interest. As you pay down the balance, more goes to principal. This is why extra payments early in your loan have the biggest impact.
Private Mortgage Insurance (PMI) is required when your down payment is less than 20%. It typically costs 0.5% to 1% of your loan amount annually.

When comparing 15-year vs 30-year mortgages: 15-year loans have higher monthly payments but significantly lower total interest. A $400,000 loan at 7% (30-year) vs 6.5% (15-year) saves over $330,000 in interest.

faqs.question: How much house can I afford?
faqs.answer: A general rule is that monthly housing costs shouldn't exceed 28% of gross income. Total debt payments shouldn't exceed 36%.

faqs.question: What's included in a mortgage payment?
faqs.answer: Principal, Interest, Taxes, and Insurance (PITI). If your down payment is under 20%, you may also pay PMI.

faqs.question: How do extra payments affect my mortgage?
faqs.answer: Extra payments go directly toward principal, reducing the amount that accrues interest and shortening your payoff date.

faqs.question: What credit score do I need?
faqs.answer: Conventional loans typically require 620+, FHA loans accept 580+ (3.5% down). Higher scores get better rates.

faqs.question: Should I get pre-approved first?
faqs.answer: Yes! Pre-approval shows sellers you're serious and helps you understand your budget before house hunting.

educationalContent.title: Understanding Calories
paragraphs: A calorie is a unit of energy. Your body needs a certain number of calories each day to function—this is your Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE). Eating fewer calories than your TDEE creates a deficit and leads to weight loss.
The Mifflin-St Jeor equation is considered the most accurate for estimating Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR). Your TDEE is then calculated by multiplying BMR by an activity factor.

For weight loss, a deficit of 500 calories per day typically results in about 1 pound of weight loss per week. For muscle gain, a surplus of 250-500 calories supports growth without excessive fat gain.

Quality of calories matters too. 2000 calories from whole foods provides different nutrition than 2000 calories from processed foods. Focus on protein, fiber, and micronutrients alongside your calorie target.

faqs.question: How many calories should I eat to lose weight?
faqs.answer: For safe weight loss, eat 500 fewer calories than your TDEE. This typically results in 1 pound of weight loss per week.

faqs.question: What's the minimum calories I should eat?
faqs.answer: Women should generally eat at least 1200 calories; men at least 1500. Going below this can cause nutrient deficiencies.

faqs.question: How accurate are calorie calculators?
faqs.answer: Calculators provide estimates. Individual metabolism varies. Track your intake and weight for 2-3 weeks to find your true needs.

faqs.question: Should I eat back exercise calories?
faqs.answer: Generally, eat back about half of exercise calories. Fitness trackers often overestimate calorie burn.

faqs.question: Do calories matter more than macros?
faqs.answer: For weight change, total calories are most important. For body composition and health, macro balance matters too.

educationalContent.title: About Age Calculation
paragraphs: Age calculation seems simple but has interesting nuances. In most Western countries, you're considered 0 years old at birth and turn 1 on your first birthday.

Some cultures count age differently. In traditional Korean age counting, babies are 1 at birth and everyone gains a year on New Year's Day. This means you could be up to 2 years 'older' in Korean age.
The exact age calculation accounts for leap years, varying month lengths, and time zones. Our calculator handles all these complexities to give you precise results.
Age milestones vary by culture. While 18 or 21 often marks adulthood in Western countries, other cultures celebrate different ages as significant transitions.

faqs.question: How do you calculate exact age?
faqs.answer: We subtract your birthdate from today, accounting for leap years and varying month lengths to give years, months, and days.

faqs.question: What is Korean age?
faqs.answer: In Korean age, you're 1 at birth and gain a year each New Year's Day. You can be up to 2 years older in Korean age.

faqs.question: How do leap years affect age?

educationalContent.title: Understanding Percentages
paragraphs: A percentage is a number expressed as a fraction of 100. The word 'percent' comes from Latin 'per centum' meaning 'by the hundred.' So 50% means 50 per 100, or half.
To find X% of Y: multiply Y by X and divide by 100. For example, 20% of 80 = (20 × 80) / 100 = 16.
Percentage increase formula: ((New - Old) / Old) × 100. If a price goes from $50 to $60, that's ((60-50)/50) × 100 = 20% increase.
A common mistake: percentage points vs percentages. If interest rates go from 5% to 7%, that's a 2 percentage point increase, but a 40% increase in the rate itself.

faqs.question: How do I calculate percentage?
faqs.answer: Divide the part by the whole and multiply by 100. For example, 25/50 × 100 = 50%.

faqs.question: What is X% of Y?
faqs.answer: Multiply Y by X and divide by 100. Example: 15% of 200 = (15 × 200) / 100 = 30.

faqs.question: How do I calculate percentage increase?
faqs.answer: Subtract the old value from new, divide by old value, multiply by 100. Formula: ((New-Old)/Old) × 100.

faqs.question: How do I calculate percentage decrease?
faqs.answer: Same formula as increase: ((Old-New)/Old) × 100. The result will show the decrease.

faqs.question: What's the difference between percentage and percentage points?
faqs.answer: Percentage points measure absolute difference (5% to 8% = 3 points). Percentage measures relative change (5% to 8% = 60% increase).
